options.label: Cut the Hoist-Chain Above the Casks.
options.detail: You counted the casks, and you know where the chain runs. The barrels on the front gantry will drop into the river instead of the floor.

quote.speaker: Alf
quote.text: The chain, Mr Holmes! The one with the hook! It's up on the roof by the winch!

options.outcome: You are on the gantry before you have finished the thought, and the chain parts under the third blow of the iron bar. The front of the loft goes over into the river with a long, slow, shuddering crash. A great cloud of smoke and steam. The fire, which had the floor in its hand a moment before, is suddenly a small, sullen thing in a corner. Wiggins has the boys out of the water-door before you have taken a second breath. When the Professor looks round for his exit, there are four constables standing in it.
options.requiresFlagHint: Needs the oil counted on Monday

options.label: Run the Boys Out by the Water-Stair.
options.detail: A boy knows a stair. If there is a way out of a building, he will have found it already.

quote.speaker: Wiggins
quote.text: This way! Single file, and don't push! Alf, you're last, and you hold the rope! I said single file, Dickie!

options.outcome: They go out through the smoke by the water-stair in a long, silent, orderly line, each with a hand on the shoulder in front. They are standing in the wet on the foreshore, coughing, before the beams begin to go. Not one is missing. By the time that the Professor has come to the end of his own plan, he finds that the ground on which he is standing has been taken by the thing that he forgot to count, which is a quantity of small and angry people.
options.requiresHint: Needs Hands in hand

options.label: Go Back In for the Professor.
options.detail: A man who has set fire to his own house does not generally intend to be in it. But he may be, and you would rather not know.

quote.speaker: Professor Moriarty
quote.text: You should not have come in, Mr Holmes. I had made provision for most things, but not, I think, for you.

success.outcome: He is standing in the middle of the burning floor, with his hat in his hand, quite composed, and he lets you take him by the sleeve as a gentleman allows a waiter to take his coat. You get him to the water-door with a beam coming down behind you, and the last you see of the warehouse is the whole of the roof going up like a lantern.

failure.outcome: The smoke closes over you, and you go down on your knees, with the floor hot under your palms. The Professor's figure on the far side of the fire turns, with a slight, courteous inclination of the head, and is lost. You are got out by a boy of eleven, by the coat. He has saved your life, and he is not at all impressed by it.

options.label: Leave Him to the Fire and Get the Boys Out.
options.detail: It is not a victory. But a child is not a thing to be set on a scale.

quote.speaker: Wiggins
quote.text: Mr Holmes, we've all got out. Every one. We've not got him, but we've got the boys.

options.outcome: You do the only thing that a man can do, and you do it without hesitation, and the Professor, in the smoke, has gone. When the fire has burnt down, there is nothing in the ruin of the warehouse but a quantity of charred oak and a small, neat, empty chair, in the middle of the floor, that no fire has touched.

M9.title: One Throw More
M9.description:
Friday 1 May, the late afternoon. The Cabinet Room is empty but for your brother, and the Prime Minister's secretary, and a tea-tray that no one has touched. The first throw has missed. It was a good one, and it was made at the right time, and it has not worked, and for a moment you stand and look at the table.

Then Mycroft, who has not moved from his chair, says, in his flat, slow voice, that the Government has not yet decided that it is beaten, and that there is a quarter of an hour before the Prime Minister's carriage is called. He says it as one would give a man a coin for the omnibus. You have, therefore, exactly one more.

options.label: Lay the Professor's Cables Before the Committee.
options.detail: You broke the cipher. Every cable of the year, in plain English, with the Professor's own dates. There is nothing the Government can say to that.

quote.speaker: Mycroft Holmes
quote.text: You had them all along, Sherlock, and you kept them in your waistcoat for a week. I do not know whether to be proud of you or to dismiss you from the service. I shall do neither. Hand them to Sir Edward.

options.outcome: The sheets go on the green cloth in order, and Sir Edward reads the first aloud. By the sixth he has put down his tea. By the tenth the Prime Minister has been sent for, in the middle of his dinner, and has come, with a napkin in his collar. There is a warrant by seven, and a van by nine, and a quiet corridor in Holloway by midnight.

options.label: Put the Second Ledger in Lestrade's Hands.
options.detail: If the Government will not use it, the Yard will. Lestrade is a man who knows what to do with a ledger, and what not to say about it.

quote.speaker: Inspector Lestrade
quote.text: You want me to take it to the Commissioner, Mr Holmes, with the Government's name written in it. I'll do it.

options.outcome: He walks out of the Cabinet Room with the ledger under his arm and his hat on straight, past the secretary, past the doorkeeper, past a Cabinet minister who tries to say something and is passed too. By the next morning it is the property of the Metropolitan Police, and by the next week it is in the hands of a printer.
options.requiresHint: Needs the second ledger read and Lestrade's trust

options.label: Ask Greaves to Watch the Channel Ports Himself.
options.detail: He will have men at Dover, Southampton, Folkestone and Newhaven by midnight. There are not many places in England from which a man of his height can leave unobserved.

quote.speaker: Superintendent Greaves
quote.text: Every port on the south coast, sir, and a man at every station. I do not say we shall have him. I say that he will have to be a remarkable gentleman to get past thirty.

success.outcome: It is a telegram, at three in the morning, from a station-master at Newhaven. A tall, stooping gentleman has taken a first-class ticket for Dieppe under the name of Mr Alexander Bell, with a violin-case. He is stopped at the barrier by a young man from Special Branch with a cold. He goes quietly. He asks only whether there will be time for him to finish his tea.

failure.outcome: He is not at any of them. He left London on the Wednesday, in a plain brougham, with a quiet, plausible gentleman who is understood to be a clergyman, and he has been in Calais since Thursday. The ports are watched with great care for a week, and nothing at all is seen, except a number of tall, stooping, innocent men.

options.label: Let the Professor Sail.
options.detail: There is no more to be done tonight, and you have had the better part of a week of it.

quote.speaker: Mycroft Holmes
quote.text: You are doing the sensible thing, Sherlock. It is the only thing in the world that I should like less than to see you do.

options.outcome: You rise from the table, and your brother does not, and the Prime Minister's secretary looks at his watch. There is nothing to say. You go out into Whitehall in a fine rain, and find that the lamps have been lit. Somewhere to the south, a long way off, a ship's siren sounds, low, like a large animal clearing its throat.

LORE_CITY_MISFORTUNES.headline: A SEASON OF MISFORTUNES IN THE CITY
LORE_CITY_MISFORTUNES.bodyText:
LONDON, Friday. The Lord Mayor's office has received, in the last three weeks, no fewer than forty-one complaints touching irregularities in the discount market, the Lombard Street banks and the Hatton Garden jewellers. Each case, on examination, has proved to be a separate affair. Each has been referred to a separate division of the police. A Cornhill broker, who asked that his name should not be printed, observed that the City was being 'nibbled, sir, as a cheese is nibbled, by a small mouse that has never once been seen.'

MEANWHILE, in Baker Street, the lamp in a certain first-floor window has been seen burning at four in the morning for six nights together. Neighbours decline to comment.

TRANSITION_YARD.headline: SCOTLAND YARD TO 221B BAKER STREET
TRANSITION_YARD.bodyText: RECEIVED 11.52 P.M. FRIDAY. ASSISTANT COMMISSIONER WILL SEE YOU SATURDAY, TEN O'CLOCK, FIRST FLOOR, LONG ROOM. BRING EVERYTHING. BRING WHATEVER YOU HAVE ON THE PROFESSOR, AND WHATEVER YOU CAN PROVE. THE CHIEF IS SCEPTICAL BUT WILL LISTEN. IF YOU ARE WRONG THIS WILL FINISH US BOTH. LESTRADE.

TRANSITION_STREET.headline: FROM WIGGINS, IN PENCIL
TRANSITION_STREET.bodyText: DEAR MR HOLMES WE HAVE GOT THE MAP DONE. ITS ON THE KITCHEN TABLE. ELEVEN HOUSES AND A DOG. THE BOYS SAY THEY WILL NOT SLEEP TILL ITS FINISHED AND I HAVE TOLD THEM NOT TO BE SILLY BUT THEY WILL. PLEASE COME QUICK. W. WIGGINS. P.S. MRS HUDSON SAYS WILL YOU WIPE YOUR FEET.

TRANSITION_CONTINENT.headline: THE CONTINENTAL EXPRESS: A WARNING TO TRAVELLERS
TRANSITION_CONTINENT.bodyText:
VICTORIA, Saturday. The boat-train for Dover, Calais and the Continent will run as usual this morning, though travellers are advised that the line near Canterbury has been much occupied of late with special trains. The company regrets the inconvenience.

A CORRESPONDENT writes that on Friday evening an elderly gentleman, with a stoop and a broad-brimmed hat, was observed at the Charing Cross Hotel in earnest conversation with a young physician. The gentleman, our correspondent adds, 'was a good deal more cheerful than his years would warrant.'

TRANSITION_REICHENBACH.headline: THE FALLS OF THE REICHENBACH
TRANSITION_REICHENBACH.bodyText: A MILE and a half above Meiringen, the Reichenbach, a stream of considerable volume, descends in a series of leaps into a narrow and exceedingly deep gorge. The best view is obtained from a path cut into the rock above the principal fall, which the traveller will find slippery in wet weather, and in places so narrow that two persons cannot walk abreast. The roar of the water is deafening. Visitors are earnestly requested not to approach the edge.

CRISIS_EVIDENCE.headline: THERE IS NOTHING IN THE FILE
CRISIS_EVIDENCE.bodyText: You read through your own notes for the third time tonight, and the same thing happens that happened the first and the second. Every link in the chain is sound, and not one is proved. A witness has been frightened off. A ledger has been shown to be a copy. A date has been found to be wrong by a day. If you are to take the Professor in a court of law, you will have to find something he cannot explain away, and soon. The case is hanging by a thread, and he knows exactly where the thread is.

CRISIS_STANDING.headline: A GENTLEMAN WHO SEES CONSPIRACIES: THE POLICE GROW WEARY
CRISIS_STANDING.bodyText: A good deal of private irritation has been expressed, in the corridors of Scotland Yard, at the activities of a certain gentleman in Baker Street, who is understood to have a theory of an elaborate criminal conspiracy underlying half the commercial misfortunes of the metropolis. Officers of experience observe that the gentleman has not yet produced a conviction. A senior inspector remarked, 'We are always glad of a clever man. We are less glad when the clever man is wrong, and louder.'

CRISIS_NERVE.headline: FROM A PRIVATE NOTEBOOK, NEVER PUBLISHED
CRISIS_NERVE.bodyText: He has not slept. I have watched him for three nights now, and I do not think he has slept for more than an hour in the stretch. He sits with his knees drawn up and his violin on the floor, and his face has gone the grey of old paper. When I speak to him he turns his head slowly, like a man who has forgotten the way. I know the look. I have seen it in the wards. Someone must make him rest, and I do not think it will be me, because he will not listen.

TRANSITION_MYCROFT.headline: THE DIOGENES CLUB
TRANSITION_MYCROFT.bodyText: MR MYCROFT HOLMES requests the favour of Mr Sherlock Holmes's company at the Club, on Saturday, at eleven in the morning. Mr Holmes will be received in the Strangers' Room, where conversation is permitted. He is requested to arrive punctually, to be brief, and to say nothing that he would not wish to see in the Estimates. The Club regrets that it cannot offer refreshment. It regrets very little else.

TRANSITION_HIATUS.headline: SHERLOCK HOLMES: AN APPRECIATION
TRANSITION_HIATUS.bodyText:
THE news from Switzerland has been received in London with a general sorrow. Mr Sherlock Holmes, who was understood to have fallen with the notorious Professor Moriarty at the Falls of the Reichenbach on Monday last, was the most remarkable private detective of our time, and, those who knew him will say, among the most remarkable men. He was reserved, brilliant, and, it was sometimes thought, a little cold. It is to be hoped that it will be possible to say, in the years to come, that he was also happy.

His friend and companion, Dr John Watson, has declined to comment.

CRISIS_HOURS.headline: THE LAST TRAIN IS GONE
CRISIS_HOURS.bodyText:
DOWN TRAINS. Victoria to Dover, 9.45 a.m., 12.30 p.m., 4.15 p.m. Passengers are requested to observe that the last connection of the day leaves at a quarter past four, and that no train is held for any person whatever.

There was always one more thing to do. You did it, and then another, and by the time you looked up the afternoon had gone. Whatever you are late for, you are late for it now.

CRISIS_HANDS.headline: FROM WIGGINS, IN PENCIL
CRISIS_HANDS.bodyText: MR HOLMES THE BOYS HAVE GONE HOME. I TOLD THEM TO. THEY WERE TIRED AND SOME OF THEM WERE SCARED AND I DID NOT THINK YOU WOULD MIND. I AM SORRY. THERE IS NOBODY LEFT TO SEND. W.

CRISIS_WIRES.headline: NO MESSAGE RECEIVED
CRISIS_WIRES.bodyText: TO MR S HOLMES 221B BAKER STREET. THE POST OFFICE REGRETS THAT THE WIRES TO YOUR DISTRICT ARE DOWN. YOUR MESSAGES OF FRIDAY AND SATURDAY HAVE NOT BEEN DELIVERED. NO REPLY WILL BE EXPECTED.

TRANSITION_BOHEMIA.headline: A GENTLEMAN WILL CALL AT A QUARTER TO EIGHT
TRANSITION_BOHEMIA.bodyText: There will call upon you to-night, at a quarter to eight o'clock, a gentleman who desires to consult you upon a matter of the very deepest moment. Your recent services to one of the Royal Houses of Europe have shown that you are one who may safely be trusted with matters which are of an importance which can hardly be exaggerated. This account of you we have from all quarters received. Be in your chamber then at that hour, and do not take it amiss if your visitor wear a mask.

TRANSITION_BAND.source: A Telegram, Handed In at Leatherhead
TRANSITION_BAND.headline: COMING BY THE EARLY TRAIN
TRANSITION_BAND.bodyText: MR HOLMES. A YOUNG LADY WILL CALL UPON YOU THIS MORNING AT A QUARTER PAST SEVEN. SHE IS IN GREAT TROUBLE AND HAS NOBODY TO GO TO. SHE ASKS THAT YOU WILL NOT LET HER LEAVE THE HOUSE UNTIL SHE HAS TOLD YOU EVERYTHING. HER MOTHER IS DEAD AND HER SISTER IS DEAD AND SHE IS VERY AFRAID. SHE ASKS FOR NO DOCTOR. A FRIEND.

TRANSITION_CARBUNCLE.headline: THE COSMOPOLITAN JEWEL ROBBERY
TRANSITION_CARBUNCLE.bodyText: John Horner, a plumber, aged thirty, was brought up at the Bow Street Police Court on the charge of having abstracted from the jewel-case of the Countess of Morcar the valuable gem known as the blue carbuncle. James Ryder, the upper-attendant at the hotel, gave evidence of having shown Horner up to the dressing-room of the Countess in order that he might solder the second bar of the grate, which was loose. He had remained with Horner for some time, but had finally been called away. On returning he found that Horner had disappeared, that the bureau had been forced open, and that the small morocco casket in which, as it afterwards transpired, the Countess was accustomed to keep her jewel, was lying empty upon the dressing-table. The prisoner was committed for trial.

TRANSITION_LEAGUE.source: The Morning Post, a small advertisement
TRANSITION_LEAGUE.headline: TO THE RED-HEADED LEAGUE
TRANSITION_LEAGUE.bodyText: On account of the bequest of the late Ezekiah Hopkins, of Lebanon, Pennsylvania, U.S.A., there is now another vacancy open which entitles a member of the League to a salary of four pounds a week for purely nominal services. All red-headed men who are sound in body and mind, and above the age of twenty-one years, are eligible. Apply in person on Monday, at eleven o'clock, to Duncan Ross, at the offices of the League, 7 Pope's Court, Fleet Street.

DEADLINE_RAIDS_LATE.headline: THE RAIDS WENT OFF WITHOUT YOU
DEADLINE_RAIDS_LATE.bodyText: LESTRADE HAS NOT WAITED. THE ELEVEN HOUSES WERE ENTERED AT HALF PAST THREE, WHICH IS EARLIER THAN WE AGREED, BECAUSE THE SUPERINTENDENT WOULD NOT HOLD HIS MEN ANOTHER HOUR ON YOUR ACCOUNT. HALF THE BIRDS WERE ALREADY GONE. I AM SORRY. I DID SAY THAT YOU WERE SLOW. L.

DEADLINE_RAIDS_EARLY.headline: A DAY IN HAND
DEADLINE_RAIDS_EARLY.bodyText: For once you are ahead of the hour. The warrants are signed, the men are fed, and Lestrade, who has been up since four, has been told that he may sleep until two. It is a small, rare, rather astonishing thing, to find that the day has been waiting for you, and not the other way round.

DEADLINE_TIDE_LATE.headline: THE TEAL CAME UP EARLY
DEADLINE_TIDE_LATE.bodyText: MR HOLMES THE BARGE IS IN. SHE CAME UP ON THE TIDE A QUARTER HOUR BEFORE YOU SAID AND SOMEBODY IS ALREADY ON THE STAIRS. I DID NOT LIKE TO SEND THE BOYS IN WITHOUT YOU. WE ARE BEHIND. W.

DEADLINE_TIDE_EARLY.headline: YOU ARE ON THE STAIRS FIRST
DEADLINE_TIDE_EARLY.bodyText: The tide has not yet turned and the wharf is still. You have time to count the boys twice, to look at the water, and to find the dry place on the third step where a man might stand and not be seen from the door. For the first time in a week the river is on your side.

DEADLINE_HOTEL_LATE.headline: THE GENTLEMAN HAS ARRIVED
DEADLINE_HOTEL_LATE.bodyText: A gentleman, Monsieur, came by the noon diligence, a good deal earlier than anyone supposed, and has asked the way to the Falls. He gave no name. He has left his bag at the desk. It is a small bag. The porter would be most obliged if you would say whether he is to be given a room.

DEADLINE_HOTEL_EARLY.headline: A QUIET MORNING
DEADLINE_HOTEL_EARLY.bodyText: It is an odd thing to record, but Holmes slept until seven, and ate a roll, and sat for twenty minutes at the window with the Alps in the glass, saying nothing whatever. He had everything arranged by nine. I have not seen him so easy since the spring, and I find that it makes me more anxious, not less.

DEADLINE_CABINET_LATE.headline: THE CABINET SAT WITHOUT YOU
DEADLINE_CABINET_LATE.bodyText: THE PRIME MINISTER HAS TAKEN THE QUESTION AT NOON, AS HE SAID HE WOULD, AND AS YOU WERE NOT HERE HE HAS TAKEN IT ON YOUR BROTHER'S WORD ALONE. I HAVE DONE WHAT I COULD. I SHOULD HAVE BEEN GLAD OF A DAY MORE, AND SO, I DARE SAY, WOULD YOU. M.

DEADLINE_CABINET_EARLY.headline: THE CABINET WILL WAIT FOR YOU
DEADLINE_CABINET_EARLY.bodyText: THE PRIME MINISTER HAS PUT BACK THE QUESTION TO THE AFTERNOON AT MY REQUEST, AND ASKS ME TO SAY THAT HE WILL BE GLAD TO HEAR YOU FULLY. IT IS NOT A THING I HAVE ASKED OF HIM BEFORE. YOU HAVE ARRIVED, I NOTICE, A DAY EARLY. IT SUITS YOU. M.

ANSWER_CABS.headline: THE CAB AT THE CORNER WAS A DECOY
ANSWER_CABS.bodyText: You stopped the yard in Kentish Town. He sold it on the Thursday to a man in Hackney who has never driven a horse, and moved the one cab that mattered to the next street, where it is waiting now, with its lamps out and a rug over the wheel. It was done quietly, and for a price, and nobody in the yard will say who paid it.

ANSWER_MOLE.source: The Home Office, an internal minute
ANSWER_MOLE.headline: A NEW MAN AT THE YARD
ANSWER_MOLE.bodyText: You put your finger on the Yard's informer, and the Yard thanked you, and dismissed him. The Professor sent his regrets and, by the same post, a young man with excellent references who has been sitting in the second-floor room since Tuesday. Nobody has yet found out why the young man's references are so good.

ANSWER_PAPER.headline: THE PAPER IS PRINTED ELSEWHERE
ANSWER_PAPER.bodyText: You turned the printer, and the printer was grateful and frightened, and told you what he knew. It has made no difference. The Professor's pamphlets are coming off another press in a cellar in Southwark, a better press, in a better ink, and the lies in them are better lies. Nobody in Fleet Street is aware that the press has changed.

ANSWER_BANK.headline: THE MONEY HAS MOVED
ANSWER_BANK.bodyText: You ran the bank, and the bank was run, and every account that you could find was empty by Wednesday. The lieutenants have been paid in coin and told to carry what they need. The Professor has no more use for Lombard Street. And a boy who did an errand for you at the back door of the bank on Wednesday is not at his lodging tonight.

ANSWER_CABLES.source: Mr Fenn, at the cable room
ANSWER_CABLES.headline: THE CIPHER CHANGED ON MONDAY
ANSWER_CABLES.bodyText: You read the whole of a year of his cables, and it was the finest thing that you have done. On Monday he changed the key. It is a new page, and a new book, and a new hour of the day, and Mr Fenn is looking at a column of four-figure groups again with the face of a man who has been told that the shore has moved. The year is read. It is a year old.

ENDING_CRISIS_EVIDENCE.title: The Case Collapses
ENDING_CRISIS_EVIDENCE.headline: FAMOUS DETECTIVE'S 'NAPOLEON' CALLED A FANCY: THE PROFESSOR THANKS THE POLICE
ENDING_CRISIS_EVIDENCE.text: It goes slowly, and then all at once. A witness retracts. A ledger is found to be a copy, and the copy a forgery. A bank-book that should have hanged a man is found to be in the wrong year. By the time the Assistant Commissioner closes the file, there is nothing left in it that a jury would look at twice. Professor Moriarty is invited to dine with the Lord Mayor in the autumn, and sends his regrets. You are not invited anywhere. In Baker Street the files lie where you left them, and every one of them is perfectly true, and not one of them can be proved.

variants.headline: WARRANTS QUASHED: THE YARD DROPS THE MORIARTY INQUIRY
variants.text: The warrants are quashed one by one in the week before Whitsun. The magistrate who signs the last of them says, kindly, that he has never doubted your good faith, and Lestrade stands behind you in the corridor, looking at his boots. Eleven addresses were searched. Not one of them is mentioned in the order that closes the file.

variants.headline: A WAR WITHOUT A FILE: NOTHING FOR A COURT
variants.text: There is nothing in the boys' notebooks that a court would hear: a dozen children's pencil-lists, a map in coloured chalk, and a ledger of dates that every barrister in London would call hearsay. The Professor's organisation does not so much as shake. Wiggins asks, once, whether it was all for nothing. You tell him that it was not. It is not a convincing answer.

variants.headline: THE STATE HAD EVERYTHING BUT A FACT
variants.text: Whitehall has all the power in England and not one fact it can use. Mycroft closes the file with a small, tired movement of the hand. 'We shall have to wait,' he says, 'for him to make a mistake. He has not made one since 1885.' The Cabinet Room is thanked, and dismissed, and the Professor dines out on the Friday.

variants.headline: FROM SWITZERLAND: A CASE LEFT BEHIND IN LONDON
variants.text: You are in a Swiss hotel with a trunk of papers and no case. The telegrams from London say only that the arrests have been released for want of evidence. You read them in silence, one after another, and Watson, across the table, does not ask. The river goes on outside the window, loud and white and entirely unconcerned.

variants.headline: IT NEVER BEGAN: THE FILE ON THE PROFESSOR IS A HEAP OF CUTTINGS
variants.text: It ends before it has properly begun. By April the file is a heap of cuttings and a name nobody will repeat, and the Yard, which never opened a door to you, closes it politely. You were right about everything. It is a poor thing to have been, in the circumstances, and a quiet one.

ENDING_CRISIS_STANDING.title: The Discredited Detective
ENDING_CRISIS_STANDING.headline: BAKER STREET 'CONSULTANT' WARNED BY MAGISTRATE: A MAN WHO SEES CONSPIRACIES
ENDING_CRISIS_STANDING.text: A man may be right a hundred times and wrong once, and the world will remember only the once. By the end of the month there is a paragraph in the Standard, a joke in Punch, a letter from the Home Office and a visit from a quiet gentleman of the Yard. You are told, with every courtesy, that the Metropolitan Police will no longer be requiring your assistance. The clients stop coming. The telegrams stop coming. The Professor, meanwhile, has taken a villa at Sevenoaks and is said to be writing a book. You play the violin, and the street below goes by without looking up.

variants.headline: SCOTLAND YARD: NO FURTHER CONTACT WITH MR HOLMES
variants.text: Lestrade is the last to go. He comes to Baker Street on a wet evening in May to say, awkwardly, that the Chief has forbidden further contact, and that he has never in his life been so ashamed of an order. He does not stay for tea. At the door he turns and says that he, for one, never doubted a word. Nobody says anything kinder to you that year.

variants.headline: A GENTLEMAN WITH AN ARMY OF CHILDREN: THE YARD TAKES NOTICE
variants.text: The Yard decides, at last, that a gentleman who commands an army of street children is a gentleman to be watched. Two constables are posted at the corner of Baker Street. They are, you realise, not there to protect you. Wiggins and the boys are not seen again at the area door, and nobody tells you where they have gone, and you do not ask.

variants.headline: WHITEHALL FORGETS
variants.text: Whitehall forgets you with an elegance that is almost beautiful. The doors do not shut. They simply cease to be there. At the Diogenes Club a servant tells you, in a low voice, that Mr Mycroft is from home, and has been for some time. You stand on the steps in the rain, a man who was, a month ago, a person of consequence.

variants.headline: 'HOLMES FLEES': THE PAPERS HAVE IT AT LAST
variants.text: The London papers have found you out. 'HOLMES FLEES', says the Standard, in an inch of black type, and the Professor's friends supply the rest. You are a fugitive from your own reputation, in a foreign hotel, with a revolver and a friend. Watson reads the paper aloud to you in a flat, steady voice, and when he has finished he folds it, and says that he has never believed a word.

variants.headline: A WORD, A PARAGRAPH, A POLITE REFUSAL
variants.text: It does not take long. A paragraph, a rumour, a polite refusal at the Yard. By Easter the notes on the mantelpiece have stopped coming, and Mrs Hudson has begun to dust the pipe-rack with the air of a woman clearing a room for a funeral. You are the cleverest man in London, and nobody wants to hear it.

ENDING_CRISIS_NERVE.title: The Black Dog
ENDING_CRISIS_NERVE.headline: CELEBRATED DETECTIVE TAKEN ILL: DOCTOR FORBIDS ALL VISITORS
ENDING_CRISIS_NERVE.text: There is a limit to what a mind can do without sleep, and you have been past it since March. It comes in the small hours, in a silence so total that you hear the blood in your ears: a heaviness, a sullen refusal of the machine to turn. You sit in the chair and cannot rise. Watson comes at dawn with his bag and his grave, tired face, and sits with you through the morning, and says nothing that is not kind. The Professor has won nothing. He has only waited. A man who has driven himself so hard, you understand, needs no enemy in the end.

variants.headline: ON THE MORNING OF THE RAIDS: A GREAT DETECTIVE TAKEN ILL
variants.text: It comes on the morning of the raids. You stand at the long table at Scotland Yard with eleven warrants in front of you and cannot read the first of them. Lestrade takes you by the elbow, gently, and says that he will see to it. He does see to it. The raids go forward, and the net closes, and you are not there to see it.

variants.headline: THE BOYS TAKE OVER: A CELLAR IN LISSON GROVE
variants.text: The boys find you in the cellar of the Lisson Grove lodging, sitting on an upturned crate with a candle and your hands in your lap. Wiggins takes off his cap. 'Mr Holmes,' he says, low. 'Mr Holmes. We'll take it from here.' They carry you up the stair between them, five small figures and one tall one, with a great deal of whispering.

variants.headline: A VAST PATIENT FIGURE BY THE WINDOW
variants.text: Mycroft finds you on the steps of the Treasury at four in the morning. He does not ask. He takes you home in a closed carriage, puts you to bed, and for three days sits in the chair by the window, a vast patient figure, reading the Gazette. When you wake he says only that he has cancelled the Cabinet, and that you are not to be thanked for it.

variants.headline: A HOTEL IN GENEVA: A DOCTOR WRITES TO LONDON
variants.text: In the Geneva hotel you wake in the dark and cannot remember the name of the town. Watson, in the next room, hears you speaking to the wall. He sits with you until the morning, and then he writes, in cipher, to your brother. The Falls are three days off. You will not see them.

variants.headline: AN ARMCHAIR, A MORNING, A CAB
variants.text: It is not dramatic. You simply cannot get out of the chair. Watson finds you at nine, grey and silent among the papers, and sends Mrs Hudson for a cab. The case, which you had thought so large, turns out to have been a great deal smaller than the man who was trying to carry it.

ENDING_NET_CLOSES.title: The Net Closes
ENDING_NET_CLOSES.headline: NAPOLEON OF CRIME TAKEN AT LAST: PROFESSOR MORIARTY IN CUSTODY
ENDING_NET_CLOSES.text: The trial at the Old Bailey lasts eleven days. Professor Moriarty stands in the dock with his hands folded, a tall, patient, scholarly figure, and listens to the whole of it with the attentive politeness of a man at a lecture. When the verdict is read he inclines his head, as if to a colleague whose argument he had expected. The sentence is penal servitude for life. In the weeks that follow, the network that took ten years to build falls into pieces, and a hundred small crimes across London simply stop. Lestrade shakes your hand on the steps of the court. 'I'll not say I understood it,' he says. 'But I'll say it was done right.'

variants.headline: THE LAW AT LAST: A CLAUSE KEPT
variants.text: The trial is held in public, at the Old Bailey, in the first week of June, because you insisted on a clause and your brother, who has never in his life been outflanked, was outflanked. The Professor stands in the dock with his hands folded and his head swaying slowly from side to side, and he listens to every word of it as if it were a lecture. The Government sits on its hands in the gallery, and nearly all of it is spared. It is the cleanest victory of your career, and you feel not the least inclined to enjoy it.

variants.headline: TWELVE BOYS ON THE ROOFS: THE NET CLOSES
variants.text: The Professor is taken on the towpath at three in the morning with a carpet-bag in his hand. It is the boys who saw him first, twelve small whistles passed from slate to slate down the length of the street. Wiggins is thanked in the Commissioner's own office, in a clean collar. He tells the story for the rest of his life, with the twelve boys, and the whistles, and the Commissioner's handshake, and he never once says that he was frightened.

variants.headline: A SINGLE DOOR, A SINGLE GUESS
variants.text: You staked everything on the canal, and the Professor came by the canal, as he had to, a long figure on the towpath with a bag in his hand. Lestrade says afterwards that it was the finest piece of work he ever saw and the most reckless, and that he does not want to see either again. You say that it was not a guess. He says that it was. You both leave it at that.

variants.headline: THE LAW HAS ITS DAY: NO BARGAIN WITH THE PROFESSOR
variants.text: The trial lasts eleven days, and it is held in public, to the last witness, because you refused your brother's quiet arrangement. The names in the Professor's second ledger are read out in open court, and two Members of Parliament resign before the week is out. The Government is furious. The press is rapturous. You receive a short note from Mycroft, written in a hand that is noticeably less steady than usual. It says only: 'You were right, and I shall never forgive you.' The Professor goes down for life, and so, in due course, do eleven men of rank.

variants.headline: A TRAITOR IN THE YARD AND A NAPOLEON IN THE DOCK
variants.text: The trial lasts eleven days. The Professor is convicted, and so is Sergeant Pike, who sells the Yard's secrets in the same dock. The Yard is ashamed and grateful in about equal measure, and the shame lasts longer. Lestrade is made Chief Inspector. You are asked to dinner by people who would not have asked you in January. It is a victory that leaves a taste in the mouth: the net is closed, and a good many hands have been burned by it.

variants.headline: A QUIET WORD IN WHITEHALL, AND THE NET CLOSES
variants.text: The trial lasts eleven days, and it runs more smoothly than a trial of its kind has any right to. Doors open. Witnesses arrive. A file that was lost is found again. You know whom to thank, and you know that one day you will be asked to return the favour. The Professor is sentenced to penal servitude for life, and Lestrade shakes your hand on the court steps, and does not ask why the road was so clear.

ENDING_NAPOLEON_ESCAPES.title: The Napoleon Escapes
ENDING_NAPOLEON_ESCAPES.headline: GREAT ROUND-UP AT SCOTLAND YARD: PRINCIPAL STILL AT LARGE
ENDING_NAPOLEON_ESCAPES.text: The gang is broken, and the Professor is not. The newspapers print the numbers: thirty-one arrested, nineteen convicted, a bishop's secretary in the dock. Of the man whose organisation it was, they print only a name, and a question. He is believed to have left England. He is believed to be in Lisbon, or Vienna, or Buenos Aires. He is believed, by the more imaginative papers, to have died. You know better. Somewhere there is a mild, tall man in a quiet room who has begun again. The war is not over. It has only changed address, and you will have to follow it.

variants.headline: A MAN WHO WOULD NOT BE A SERVANT, OR A WITNESS
variants.text: You walk out of Whitehall into the sunlight, and the Professor goes on, quietly, as he has always done. The Cabinet makes its arrangements without you. The names in the black book are not printed, and not burned, and not forgotten. Mycroft, in his office, takes off his spectacles and rubs the bridge of his nose and says to nobody at all that he had not thought you would do it. It is a quiet end to a noisy year.

variants.headline: THE WAR ENDS WITHOUT AN END
variants.text: The Professor goes down the river in the dark, and you let him, and walk the length of Narrow Street with Alf's name in your head. You have not won, and you have not been beaten, and there is a boy in a grave at Limehouse to tell you that it was not a game. Wiggins does not speak to you for a month. When he does, he asks only, in a small voice, whether it was worth it. You tell him that you do not know. You have not said anything so true to him in a year.

variants.headline: THE NET WAS DRAWN. THE FISH WERE NOT ALL IN IT
variants.text: The lieutenants go to prison for ten years, fifteen years, life. The Professor goes nowhere at all. The Yard's inquiries lead to Calais, then to Marseilles, then into a long, grey silence. Lestrade says it was a fine piece of work. You say that it was half a piece of work. You are both right. The Professor's chair stands empty in his study at Kensington, with the chess game unfinished, and black to move.

variants.headline: A BROTHER WHO KNEW WHERE
variants.text: The Professor leaves England by a route that the Yard never finds. Mycroft finds it for you, and sends a single line on Foreign Office paper: 'He sailed from Antwerp on Tuesday. I thought you should know. I did not think you should do anything about it.' You keep the note in the drawer with the ledger. The war goes on, but it goes on at a distance, and your brother is now a party to it.

ENDING_REASON_OF_STATE.title: Reason of State
ENDING_REASON_OF_STATE.headline: PROFESSOR MORIARTY: A SEALED PROCEEDING AT THE OLD BAILEY
ENDING_REASON_OF_STATE.text: He is never tried in public. A closed court is convened by a judge whose name is not in the paper, in a room that does not appear on any plan of the building, and when it rises, the Professor is gone. Some say he is in Dartmoor under another name. Some say he is a guest of the Government in a house in the country. No one says that he is free, and no one says that he is not. The Prime Minister thanks you in a private letter for your discretion. Mycroft sends a case of claret. You drink none of it. Somewhere, in a locked drawer in Whitehall, a grey cloth ledger lies in the dark, and a good many men sleep a little easier.

variants.headline: SOUTHAMPTON, TUESDAY: A GENTLEMAN SAILS
variants.text: He sails on the Tuesday, in a first-class cabin, under his own name, with two trunks and a violin-case, and the newspapers say nothing, because no newspaper has been told. The names in the black book are safe, and the House of Commons sleeps quietly. Mycroft sends a case of claret, which you give to Mrs Hudson, who gives it, in turn, to the milkman. It is the nearest thing to a joke that the whole of the Moriarty business has produced.

variants.headline: THE GOVERNMENT CLOSES ITS OWN LEDGER
variants.text: You know what is in the second ledger, because Mycroft told you. You know who is in it, and why they are not in the dock. The knowledge sits in you like a cold stone. The Professor has been disposed of with every propriety, and a nation's secrets have been kept, and your brother has never in his life been so pleased with you. You wonder, in the small hours, whether you have served the law or merely the men who write it.

ENDING_PRIVATE_WAR.title: The Private War
ENDING_PRIVATE_WAR.headline: MYSTERY OF THE LIMEHOUSE WHARF: BODY OF A TALL MAN TAKEN FROM THE THAMES
ENDING_PRIVATE_WAR.text: They find him on the second morning, caught in the piles at Limehouse, and the coroner records an open verdict. There is nothing to connect the drowned man with the Professor except the shape of his forehead and the fact that, within a month, the great grey organisation of the City is in ruins. Banks close their doors. Lieutenants turn on each other. The cab-yards, the printing-shops and the public-houses are quiet. London does not know who did it. The Yard has a suspicion, and does not trouble to pursue it. You have won the war, in your own way, and the only decoration you will receive is the silence of men who prefer not to ask.

variants.headline: A WAR WON, A BOY LOST
variants.text: They find the Professor on the second morning, and a month later they find nothing at all left of his organisation. Wiggins comes to Baker Street in his best coat, and stands in the sitting-room with his cap in his hands. 'It was worth it, wasn't it, Mr Holmes?' he says. You say yes. You have told him one lie in all your life, and he knows it, and he thanks you for it. The boys never speak of Alf. They carry on, and are quiet.

variants.headline: THE IRREGULARS' VICTORY
variants.text: They find the Professor on the second morning, and a month later the whole of his organisation has dissolved like sugar in water. The Irregulars have a party, in the kitchen at Baker Street, with a ham and a cake and a barrel of ginger-beer. Alf, with his arm in a sling, makes a speech that nobody can hear for cheering. Wiggins makes you stand on a chair. You have never in your life been so embarrassed, or so happy.

variants.headline: NO ONE ASKED HOW
variants.text: The Professor is gone, and the Yard is relieved, and nobody mentions the Shoreditch counting-house or the cab-yard or the printer's shop. Lestrade comes to Baker Street, accepts a whisky, and says only that if there should be any more unfortunate accidents of the sort, it would be a kindness if the gentleman responsible would let him know in advance. You promise that there will be none. It is a promise you mean. It is also, you think, the last one you are sure of.

ENDING_BAKER_STREET_BURNS.title: Ashes in Baker Street
ENDING_BAKER_STREET_BURNS.headline: FIRE IN BAKER STREET: FAMOUS LODGINGS DESTROYED; THE PROFESSOR UNSEEN
ENDING_BAKER_STREET_BURNS.text: You are fished out at Wapping Stairs by a lighterman who takes you for a drowned seaman, and carried to a lodging-house with a cup of tea and a blanket. The house in Baker Street is a charred shell by the time you reach it. The papers are ash. The violin is a few burnt strings in the cellar. Of the Professor's organisation, the newspapers report that it has survived the police, the Yard and the Shadow War, and has emerged, if anything, stronger. London goes about its business. You stand in the wet street with Watson, and look up at the black, empty windows, and begin to think about what it is that you have left to lose.

variants.headline: BAKER STREET LOST. MRS HUDSON SAFE IN BRIGHTON
variants.text: The house is gone, and the Professor is not, and there is only one thing to be thankful for: Mrs Hudson, who is a hundred miles away in Brighton with a hamper and a cold. She comes up on the first train, in her black bonnet, and stands in the road with her hands folded. 'Seventeen steps, I counted them every morning,' she says, in a voice that is not at all steady. 'Well. They're gone now. Come along to Brighton, the pair of you, and have a decent breakfast.'

ENDING_THE_COMPACT.title: The Professor's Terms
ENDING_THE_COMPACT.headline: SOCIETY NOTES: A CELEBRATED CONSULTANT RETIRES TO THE COUNTRY
ENDING_THE_COMPACT.text: It is a handsome house, with a library and a long garden that runs down to a stream, and you are told that the money will come from a bank in Zurich. You are not told which bank. You are never asked to do anything. You are simply asked to stop, and the Professor's people, whom you pass sometimes in the lane, tip their hats with exactly the right degree of courtesy. London goes on being what it is, a little quieter, a little richer, a little more afraid. You read in the papers that a clerk has been found drowned. You turn the page. In a locked drawer you keep the grey ledger, which you have never opened again.

variants.headline: A SWISS HOLIDAY: THE DETECTIVE RETURNS ALONE
variants.text: You come down from the Falls with the Professor's paper in your coat, and a different idea of what you are. Watson never learns what passed on the path. He is told only that the Professor was not there, and that you changed your mind. You go to Interlaken. In the autumn, a house in Sussex is bought in a name that is not yours. You do not ask where the money came from, and you do not much like the look of your own face in the shaving-glass.

ENDING_THE_FALL.title: The Reichenbach Fall
ENDING_THE_FALL.headline: TERRIBLE ACCIDENT IN THE SWISS ALPS: TWO ENGLISHMEN FEARED LOST AT THE REICHENBACH FALLS
ENDING_THE_FALL.text: The guides search the gorge for three days, and find nothing. At the edge of the path above the Falls, in a patch of trodden mud, there are two sets of footprints that go to the brink and none that come back. A walking-stick leans against the rock, with a cigarette-case beneath it. In the English papers the obituary of Sherlock Holmes is a long one, and kind, and in some places wrong. The Professor's name is printed beside yours. In a village in the valley, for many years afterwards, they will point out the place to travellers, and say that two men met there, and that only the water knows what they said.

variants.headline: A LETTER FOUND ON THE PATH: DR WATSON'S LAST DUTY
variants.text: Watson finds the note at dusk, after the hotel and the empty bed and the cold evening walk back along the river. It is four lines long, folded under your case. He reads it twice by lantern-light. He sits down on the wet rock, and stays there until the guides come at midnight to take him away. In the years after, he writes the whole thing out in a clear, grave hand, and calls it the Final Problem, and does not once say what he thinks of the man who sent him to the hotel.

variants.headline: TWO ENGLISHMEN AT THE FALLS: ONE SURVIVOR
variants.text: Watson was beside you on the path, and he was the one who saw it. He tells the guides, in a flat voice, that the Professor came along the ledge, that there was a struggle, that the two men fell together. He does not say what you said before. He puts your note in his pocket-book, and carries it for the rest of his life, and when he is asked, years afterwards, whether he has ever lost a friend, he answers only that he has lost the best and the wisest man whom he has ever known.

variants.headline: A BROTHER IN BLACK
variants.text: Mycroft is told by telegram, and arrives in Meiringen on the fourth day, in a closed carriage, a great grey presence at the edge of the gorge. He says nothing at all. He looks at the water for a long while, and then at the stick, and then he asks the guides, courteously, to leave him alone. When Watson finds him he is sitting on the wet rock with his hat in his hands. It is the only time that anyone has seen the elder Holmes brother without his composure.

ENDING_THE_EMPTY_GRAVE.title: The Empty Grave
ENDING_THE_EMPTY_GRAVE.headline: HOLMES: A MEMORIAL. THE GREAT DETECTIVE'S NAME REMAINS IN BLACK
ENDING_THE_EMPTY_GRAVE.text: You decide that the dead shall stay dead. In the house in the south of France there is a chemical bench, a window on a garden, and a good view of the sea, and nobody comes to it who has any idea who you have been. The Park Lane mystery is solved by somebody else, or by nobody. The Professor's organisation is a ruin, and the Colonel is a hunted man. London goes on without Sherlock Holmes, quite as well as it did with him, and more quietly. In the evenings you play the violin, to the window, and the window does not applaud.

variants.headline: ONE MAN WHO NEVER KNEW
variants.text: You told no one at all, at the beginning, and you have kept to it. There is not a person alive who has your address. The silence has grown round you year by year, like a coat of dust on a shelf, and it has become a kind of comfort and a kind of cell. Sometimes, in the dusk, you think of Watson, and then you do not.

variants.headline: ONE MAN IN LONDON KNOWS
variants.text: Your brother's draft arrives every quarter, with a short note that says nothing. He knows where you are, and he has kept it from every living soul, including the Prime Minister. He writes in the cipher of your boyhood, and sometimes, at the foot, he writes the name of a book that he thinks you ought to read. You do not tell him that you would sooner he came to see you. It is not a thing that you say.

variants.headline: A FRIEND'S FUNERAL
variants.text: Watson came back from the hotel at the Falls and found the note, and the cigarette-case, and the stick. He did not know what to believe, so he believed the worst. You know it, and you have not written. It is a thing you tell yourself you will put right, in the spring. In the spring you tell yourself that it will be the next one.

ENDING_WATSON_STANDS.title: Two at the Falls
ENDING_WATSON_STANDS.headline: REICHENBACH TRAGEDY: THE PROFESSOR DEAD, THE DETECTIVE SAFE. COLONEL MORAN FLEES
ENDING_WATSON_STANDS.text: The guides arrive with their lanterns just after dark, and find two Englishmen sitting on a wet rock with a revolver between them. The Professor's body is found two days later at the foot of the Falls. Colonel Moran has been taken at Interlaken, in a railway carriage, with an air-gun in a violin case. In Baker Street, a month afterwards, the lamp is lit and the fire is kept, and the old armchair across the hearth is occupied again. Watson writes it all down, in his own way, and gives it to a magazine. You tell him that it is too romantic. He tells you that you are an ungrateful man. It is, you both agree, a perfectly satisfactory way to end an argument.

variants.headline: THE CASE-BOOK AND THE CARRIED LETTER
variants.text: The thirty pages you wrote at the inn are never needed. You carry them back to London in your breast-pocket and give them to Mycroft, who files them without reading, and says that it is a pity to waste such good work. Watson reads them in a night, in the old armchair, and sets them down with a face you have not seen before. 'You were prepared to die,' he says. 'You wrote it all down in case.' You tell him that you were prepared for anything. It is almost the truth.

ENDING_FATAL_SHOT.title: The Colonel's Shot
ENDING_FATAL_SHOT.headline: ENGLISH DOCTOR SHOT DEAD AT THE REICHENBACH FALLS: AIR-GUN SUSPECTED
ENDING_FATAL_SHOT.text: The report of an air-gun is small, and is lost entirely in the roar of the water. The guides, who come up with their lanterns in the early dark, find no struggle and no robbery, only a body on a rock and a living man sitting beside it, not speaking. The Professor lies at the foot of the Falls. The Colonel is taken at Interlaken three days later, quietly, in a railway carriage. It is no consolation. The war is won, and a friend is dead, and the long ride home in a first-class carriage is the quietest you have ever known.

variants.headline: DR JOHN WATSON: A SOLDIER'S DEATH
variants.text: Watson dies on the ledge, with his hand in yours, saying something about a patient in Kensington whom he has forgotten to see. It is a small, absurd, ordinary last remark, and you will remember it for the rest of your life. Mary Watson is told in London by Mycroft, who takes the news in person. You go back to Baker Street by yourself. The armchair across the hearth is the first thing you see when you light the lamp. You do not sit in your own for a long time.

variants.headline: HOLMES SHOT ON THE SWISS PATH
variants.text: You die on the ledge alone, with the last light going out of the sky and the thunder of the Falls in your ears. Watson, summoned by a false message to an empty hotel, comes up the path at nightfall and finds you gone. In a notebook, under the rock, there are four lines in your hand. He reads them. He sits down in the road. He does not get up for a long time. The world believes that the greatest detective in London met his death in a fight with the Napoleon of crime. It is, as these things go, nearly the truth.

ENDING_THE_RETURN.title: The Return to Baker Street
ENDING_THE_RETURN.headline: MR SHERLOCK HOLMES ALIVE: THE GREAT DETECTIVE RETURNS AFTER THREE YEARS
ENDING_THE_RETURN.text: The Park Lane mystery is solved within the week, and the world, which had stopped expecting anything of the sort, takes the news with a gasp. There is a long, loud, delighted correspondence in the newspapers. The Yard sends a polite note. A man who had been buried in a black border is sitting, in the same armchair, with the same pipe, in the same cloud of smoke, as if the Reichenbach Falls had been a fortnight's holiday. Mrs Hudson, on being told, puts her apron over her head and goes into the pantry, and comes out again looking very well. The rooms smell, for a month, of lavender and old books.

variants.headline: A BOOKSELLER'S SURPRISE: DR WATSON FAINTS IN HIS STUDY
variants.text: Watson tells the story of that afternoon, afterwards, to anyone who will listen, and at each telling it grows a little. He had been writing at his desk when an old bookseller came in with an armful of volumes. The bookseller had said something about a bargain, and when he looked up the bookseller was gone and in his place was a lean, pale, grinning, perfectly familiar face. 'I have never fainted in my life,' he says. 'I fainted then. And I'll thank you not to laugh.' You do not. Not very much.

variants.headline: THE LAMP LIT AND THE SUPPER LAID
variants.text: You come in with your own key, by the old stair, to the room that has not changed. Watson is in the armchair. He does not turn round. He says, in a steady voice, that you took your time, and you sit down opposite him, and neither of you says anything for the better part of an hour. It is the quietest, kindest return that a man could have had, and it is the only one that you will ever wish to remember.

variants.headline: A MAN WHO HAD ALREADY COME HOME ONCE
variants.text: You came home once before, in the dark, in a closed cab, to sit beside a friend in a silent room. Nobody knows it but the two of you. When you walk into Baker Street in the April of 1894, in plain daylight, Watson takes your hand and says only that it was a long time between visits. You say that it was. You do not say that you would have come sooner, if you had been able. He knows.

variants.headline: THE LETTER FROM FLORENCE
variants.text: Watson has the letter still. He has kept it in his pocket-book for three years, with the creases worn white, and he takes it out on the first evening, and lays it on the table between you without a word. It is four lines long. 'I had it by heart,' he says, 'in a week. I only kept it to be sure that I had not made it up.' You do not trust your voice. You pour the whisky.

variants.headline: A SUPPER FOR TWO, LAID BY A BROTHER
variants.text: Mycroft is in the sitting-room when you arrive, in your chair, with a cold supper laid for two and the air of a man who has been there since noon. 'You are late,' he says. 'I have paid your bank for three years. I do not propose to be thanked.' He is, for the first time in your memory, extremely moved. He conceals it by eating a chicken leg.

ENDING_HER_MAJESTYS_SERVICE.title: In Her Majesty's Service
ENDING_HER_MAJESTYS_SERVICE.headline: PROFESSOR MORIARTY: A QUIET END. THE NAPOLEON OF CRIME IS NO MORE
ENDING_HER_MAJESTYS_SERVICE.text: There is no trial, no headline, no inquest. A closed carriage, a closed court, and a closed file, and by Whitsun the Professor's organisation has ceased to exist, as though it had never been. You are given a small office in a street off Whitehall, with a name on the door that is not your own, and a salary that is paid by a department that does not appear in the Estimates. It is interesting work. It is not, you reflect, the kind of work that one boasts of, even to Watson, who is told only that you are engaged on 'a matter for a friend in the Government'. You keep the commission in a drawer, and you do not read it.

variants.headline: A HAND ON THE LEVER
variants.text: You hold, in a small black pocket-book, the signature of an Under-Secretary of State, and it is a thing that you will use seldom, and never lightly. It makes you a good servant to the Crown, since a man who owns a minister is a man who need never be ignored. You are good at it. You tell yourself that you will not become what you have caught. It is a thing that is easy to say in the first year.

variants.headline: A SERVANT WHO WOULD NOT READ
variants.text: You serve the Crown, and you have never opened the black book. The Crown, to its surprise, rather likes it. 'A man who has not read it,' says Mycroft, 'cannot be asked what is in it.' It is a sound principle. It lets you sleep. It is also the one thing about the whole affair that you have never been able to look at straight.

ENDING_THE_SECOND_LEDGER.title: The Second Ledger
ENDING_THE_SECOND_LEDGER.headline: THE GREAT SCANDAL: ELEVEN COLUMNS IN THE STANDARD; THREE MEMBERS RESIGN
ENDING_THE_SECOND_LEDGER.text: It is called, within a week, the Moriarty Scandal, and it runs for the whole of the summer. Three Members of Parliament resign. A bishop goes abroad. A Cabinet Minister makes a speech of three hours, and is not believed. At the end of it there is a Royal Commission, and a Bill, and a great quantity of ink. The Professor's name is spoken in the House with a kind of reluctant awe. Mycroft does not speak to you for the whole of the autumn, and then, one evening in November, he calls in a hansom without a number and says only that he has come to say that you were right, and that he cannot bear it.

variants.headline: A MINISTER WHO SPOKE FIRST
variants.text: Lord Harcastle is the only man in the book who has already confessed, and the only one who is not ruined. He gives evidence to the Commission in a low, level voice and is spared by an act of the House. It is a curious thing. You are, you find, glad for him, and a little ashamed of being so, and the two feelings sit side by side at your table for the rest of the year.

ENDING_CRISIS_STRAND.title: The Strand Snaps
ENDING_CRISIS_STRAND.headline: THE GREAT DETECTIVE OUT OF MEANS: THE PROFESSOR UNTOUCHED
ENDING_CRISIS_STRAND.text: It is not one thing but the three that hold a campaign up, and you have let one of them go. The Professor has not beaten you. He has merely outlasted you, as a tide outlasts a man with a spade.

variants.headline: TOO LATE: THE MONDAY COMES AND GOES
variants.text: There was always one more thing to do, and you did it, and then another, and by the time the last of them was done the thing it was for had already happened. The raids go off without you, or the train leaves, or the page is turned by someone else's hand. You were never wrong about anything. You were merely late for all of it, and the Professor, who has never in his life been in a hurry, has been waiting for exactly that.

variants.headline: AN EMPTY ROOM IN BAKER STREET
variants.text: At the end there is nobody left to send. Lestrade has stopped answering, the boys have been told to stay at home, Watson looks at you with a gentleness that is much worse than anger, and your brother has stopped writing. A detective is not one man. He is a system of other people's eyes and legs, and you have used them up or driven them off. You sit in a room full of the right conclusions, with no one to carry them anywhere.

variants.headline: THE LINES ARE DOWN
variants.text: It is a small silence at first: a telegram that is not answered, a letter that is not sent, a newspaper that does not call. Then it is a large one. You know a great deal, and nobody knows that you know it. The Professor has not so much cut your wires as made them irrelevant, and you sit in the middle of London with the answer in your head, as remote from the world as a man in a lighthouse.

ENDING_THE_WOMAN.title: The Woman
ENDING_THE_WOMAN.headline: BOHEMIAN SCANDAL AVERTED: A KING'S BETROTHAL ANNOUNCED
ENDING_THE_WOMAN.text: The photograph never comes home. The King is betrothed in June, to a princess of Scandinavia, and is reconciled to the thought that he has been beaten by a woman who would not have used her victory. You keep the portrait. You do not speak of her, and Watson, who is wise enough not to ask, only notices that when you are asked for a name which stands for brilliance and for grace you do not say your own. To Sherlock Holmes she is always the Woman, and the Woman, at the end of the case, is wise enough to leave the field with all her honours.

variants.headline: THE WOMAN: A WEDDING AND A FIRE
variants.text: The photograph never comes home. You have been a witness at her wedding and a casualty at her door, and you are the only man in London who knows that both were the same afternoon. The King is betrothed in June, and you keep the portrait, and Watson, who threw the rocket, will tell the story with his own part in it very much understated. To Sherlock Holmes she is always the Woman. It is a title that she has not asked for, and has earned.

variants.headline: THE WOMAN: THE LETTERS WERE BURNED
variants.text: The photograph never comes home, and neither do the letters, which the King, who told you everything, has now no reason to fear. You keep the portrait. She had a copy of the whole of it, and used none of it. You think, as you put the evening-dress photograph on your mantelpiece, that you know now what a woman can do with a weapon she has decided not to fire.

ENDING_THE_STRONGBOX.title: The Strongbox
ENDING_THE_STRONGBOX.headline: BOHEMIAN PHOTOGRAPH RECOVERED: THE LADY DEPARTS
ENDING_THE_STRONGBOX.text: You have the photograph. It lies in the lining of a book in the King's hand, and he is extremely pleased, and pays you a handsome fee, and will remember you at his coronation. You do not remember the case with the same pleasure. A woman who had done nothing was driven across a continent, and caught, and robbed, and the thing you have taken was the only thing she had left that was her own. She sends no letter. You do not look for one. It is a successful result, and it will sit in your case-book as the neatest and the least pleasant of your early cases.

variants.headline: THE STRONGBOX: A CARD LEFT ON THE MANTELPIECE
variants.text: You have the photograph, and the King has it, and the matter is closed. But on the mantelpiece of a villa in St John's Wood there is a card, with your name on it, which you left on a night that you do not wish to remember. And it is the card, rather than the photograph, which comes to your mind when you hear her name. You have won, and you are not sure of what.

ENDING_THE_KING_WAITS.title: The King Waits
ENDING_THE_KING_WAITS.headline: BETROTHAL BROKEN OFF: SCANDINAVIAN COURT SILENT
ENDING_THE_KING_WAITS.text: You did not get the photograph, and you did not tell the King. By the end of April he has heard the rest from a quarter that he has no reason to trust, and the betrothal is broken off by the Scandinavian court in a note of eleven lines. The King does not blame you in public. In private he says that he had thought you the cleverest man in Europe, and the sentence is carried to you by three separate people. It is one of the few occasions on which a woman has been wiser than Sherlock Holmes, and a king has noticed.

variants.headline: THE KING WAITS: SHE KNEW AT ONCE
variants.text: She knew from the first moment, and she let you try the whole of your plan in her drawing-room, with her maid and her coachman and a roll of smoking paper, and said nothing until you had finished. The King does not blame you in public. She, you think, has not even troubled to be amused. It is the gentlest defeat of your career, and the worst.

ENDING_THE_BAND_RETURNS.title: The Speckled Band
ENDING_THE_BAND_RETURNS.headline: SURREY TRAGEDY: DR ROYLOTT DEAD OF A SERPENT'S BITE
ENDING_THE_BAND_RETURNS.text: Dr Grimesby Roylott is found dead in his chair at Stoke Moran, with a snake coiled in his lap and a small basket at his feet. He has been killed, as he intended to kill his stepdaughter, by an Indian swamp adder, the deadliest snake in India; and it has returned, as such creatures do, to the man who feeds it. The coroner records misadventure. Helen Stoner goes to her aunt at Harrow, and is married in the autumn. You tell Watson on the train that you are, indirectly, responsible for the death of Dr Grimesby Roylott, and that you cannot say that it will weigh heavily upon your conscience.

variants.headline: THE SPECKLED BAND: THE VIGIL AND THE REVOLVER
variants.text: Dr Grimesby Roylott is found dead in his chair, with a snake in his lap and a small basket at his feet. The Surrey constabulary, who wrote it as misadventure, did not know that three men and a revolver were awake in the next room. Helen Stoner is married in the autumn. Watson dines out on the story for a year, and has the grace to omit that his hands, on the night, were not at all steady.

variants.headline: THE SPECKLED BAND: A SAUCER OF MILK
variants.text: Dr Grimesby Roylott dies of his own snake, in his own chair, and the saucer of milk on the safe is the one detail that the coroner cannot explain. You explain it to nobody. The snake, you remember, could not hear and could not see, and was taught to climb a rope by a whistle. It was an ingenious murder, and a bad idea.

ENDING_THE_WHISTLE_MISSED.title: The Whistle Missed
ENDING_THE_WHISTLE_MISSED.headline: SECOND DEATH AT STOKE MORAN: A GUEST OF THE HOUSE
ENDING_THE_WHISTLE_MISSED.text: You were a half-second late, and a half-second is all that the thing requires. By the time the lantern is lit, the damage has been done. Nobody will ever know what you intended, or why a famous detective was in the bed, or why a doctor lay across the window-sill with his hands upon his face. The inquest is open for a week. Dr Roylott gives evidence in a soft, grave, grieving voice, and the coroner thanks him for his courage. You are not at all sure that you will ever be asked to take a country case again.

variants.headline: THE WHISTLE MISSED: HE WAS WAITING
variants.text: You told him that you were coming, and he waited. It is the oldest mistake in the world, and you made it with your eyes open. The Doctor gives his evidence in a soft, grave voice, and the coroner thanks him, and the house of Stoke Moran closes its doors upon you for good.

ENDING_THE_DOCTOR_LIVES.title: A Doctor at Liberty
ENDING_THE_DOCTOR_LIVES.headline: SURREY DOCTOR EXONERATED: A DETECTIVE'S 'FANCIES'
ENDING_THE_DOCTOR_LIVES.text: The Doctor lives. The snake goes back into its basket, and the basket into the safe, and a magistrate at Leatherhead, who has dined at Stoke Moran, records that no offence was committed and that the gentleman is the victim of a mistake. Helen Stoner is moved to her aunt's at Harrow, where she is safe, and the Doctor, who is not a patient man, waits for her to marry. You are told that a detective is not a policeman. You say that you are aware of it. It is much less satisfactory than a story, and more like a life.

variants.headline: A DOCTOR AT LIBERTY: A SECOND OPINION
variants.text: The Doctor lives, and the magistrate dismisses it, but the police surgeon's note that Miss Stoner is a healthy woman in fear of her life is on the file. And a year later, when another girl is found dead in a locked room, it is the first paper that the county reads.

ENDING_THE_CHRISTMAS_MERCY.title: The Season of Forgiveness
ENDING_THE_CHRISTMAS_MERCY.headline: A COUNTESS'S JEWEL RECOVERED: THE PLUMBER CLEARED
ENDING_THE_CHRISTMAS_MERCY.text: The Countess of Morcar's blue carbuncle is returned to her on the twenty-eighth, by an anonymous messenger, and John Horner the plumber is discharged at the Old Bailey for want of a prosecutor. James Ryder is in Canada, where he is a careful man indeed. You eat your Christmas dinner a day late, with Watson and a roast goose of the second quality, and drink to a good many people who would have been surprised to hear it. Of all your cases, this is the one that you can tell at a Christmas dinner with a clear conscience.

variants.headline: THE SEASON OF FORGIVENESS: A GOOSE-CLUB DINNER
variants.text: The carbuncle goes back to the Countess, and the plumber goes home, and Henry Baker, who has been told the truth, is asked to dinner at Baker Street on New Year's Day. He brings a hat. It has been brushed. The season has no better evening.

variants.headline: THE SEASON OF FORGIVENESS: A LETTER FROM BRIXTON
variants.text: The carbuncle goes back to the Countess, and the plumber goes home. A Mrs Oakshott of the Brixton Road receives, a week after Christmas, a note and a pound. A request for the name of the best goose-farmer in Surrey. She frames the note. It is the only thing she has ever received from a celebrity.

ENDING_THE_STONE_RETURNED.title: The Law Takes Its Course
ENDING_THE_STONE_RETURNED.headline: HOTEL ATTENDANT COMMITTED FOR TRIAL: THE MORCAR JEWEL RECOVERED
ENDING_THE_STONE_RETURNED.text: James Ryder is committed for trial at the Old Bailey in February, and pleads guilty, and is given seven years. The plumber is released with the apologies of the Yard. The stone goes back to the Countess, who sends you a note of thanks in a hand like a bundle of wires. It is the correct result, and the law is satisfied; but you notice that Watson, at breakfast, is a little quiet, and that the sixth of the January newspapers is open at a column you have not read.

variants.headline: THE LAW TAKES ITS COURSE: THE FERRET IN HENRIETTA STREET
variants.text: Ryder is committed in February, and pleads guilty, and goes down for seven years. You do not often think of him. But sometimes, in a crowd at a street corner, you see a thin, frightened man in a long coat, and your arm closes round a thing that is not there.

ENDING_THE_STONE_LOST.title: The Stone Slips Away
ENDING_THE_STONE_LOST.headline: THE MORCAR CARBUNCLE: STILL MISSING
ENDING_THE_STONE_LOST.text: He ran. By the time you were in the street he was in a cab, and by the time you had a cab of your own he was lost in the Strand. The stone lies on the table, it is true, and goes back to the Countess in the morning. But the man who took it is in the wind. The plumber, who is still in gaol, will be there a fortnight longer than he need. It is a Christmas that Lestrade will not forget, and will not let you forget, either.

variants.headline: THE STONE SLIPS AWAY: THE SALESMAN KNEW
variants.text: You were turned away at the market, and you were slow to the chase, and the man who knew the end of the story was gone before you had learned the beginning. The stone goes back. The man does not. Lestrade will not let you forget it.

ENDING_THE_LEAGUE_DISSOLVED.title: The League Is Dissolved
ENDING_THE_LEAGUE_DISSOLVED.headline: THE CITY AND SUBURBAN BANK: A NARROW ESCAPE
ENDING_THE_LEAGUE_DISSOLVED.text: John Clay, murderer, thief, smasher and forger, who has for years been the cleverest criminal in London, is taken in the cellar of the City and Suburban Bank, and goes to prison for fourteen years. His accomplice is taken in the shop. Jabez Wilson goes back to his pawnbroking, with much more red in his cheeks, and takes a new assistant. Mr Merryweather sends you a cheque and a long letter. You and Watson walk home along the Embankment at three in the morning, in the first of the fog. You tell him that it is all an attempt to escape from the commonplace, and that you are glad that it has not escaped.

variants.headline: THE LEAGUE IS DISSOLVED: THE YARD'S ARREST
variants.text: John Clay is taken, with his accomplice, by Mr Peter Jones of Scotland Yard, at the end of a long evening, and the papers give the credit to Mr Jones, which is as it should be. He is promoted in the spring. You do not say a word. You think, as you walk home with Watson, that the best of a detective's work is the work that somebody else is thanked for.

variants.headline: THE LEAGUE IS DISSOLVED: A MAN WITH PIERCED EARS
variants.text: John Clay, who had been a royal duke's grandson, an Etonian, an Oxonian. A pretty hand with a spade, is taken in the cellar of the City and Suburban Bank, with the white splash of acid still upon his forehead. His ears, as you had said, are pierced for earrings. Jabez Wilson says it is a most remarkable thing that you should have noticed.

ENDING_THE_TUNNEL_OPEN.title: The Tunnel Open
ENDING_THE_TUNNEL_OPEN.headline: THIRTY THOUSAND NAPOLEONS: A CITY BANK ROBBED
ENDING_THE_TUNNEL_OPEN.text: It is the largest robbery in the City for a decade, and the whole of it has been done with a spade and a jar of paraffin and four pounds a week. The gold, thirty thousand napoleons in boxes lent by the Bank of France, has gone out through the cellar of a pawnbroker in Saxe-Coburg Square, and down the Metropolitan, and on to the Continent. John Clay is not seen again. Jabez Wilson, who had been an innocent party to the whole of it, is eventually found, in a modest lodging, in the Borough, with his hair, which is now going grey, in a small and rather sad ring. The League, you think, as you sit at the window and look at the street, was always better than the thing that it covered.

variants.headline: THE TUNNEL OPEN: A MAN WHO WENT DOWN ALONE
variants.text: The gold goes out through the tunnel in the night, and you were in the cellar when it happened, and alone, because you said you would be. It is a thing that nobody forgives. Mr Merryweather writes to the Times, in an angry and unfair hand, about private detectives who would be wiser to leave the matter to the police.

ENDING_THE_ENCYCLOPAEDIA.title: Four Pounds a Week
ENDING_THE_ENCYCLOPAEDIA.headline: A QUANTITY OF COIN MOVED FOR SECURITY
ENDING_THE_ENCYCLOPAEDIA.text: The City and Suburban Bank opens on Monday, as usual, and its customers, who have not the least idea of how near they came to being the customers of a hole in the ground, go in and out all day with their books and their bags. John Clay is in Pentonville by Tuesday. The bank does not say a word, and neither do you. Jabez Wilson, who has been told that the League was dissolved because it had served its purpose, goes back to his shop with a large and impressive volume, which he has kept, in a drawer, as a souvenir: the first volume of the Encyclopaedia Britannica, copied out in his own hand as far as the letter B, and worth, as he says, much more to him than the money.

variants.headline: FOUR POUNDS A WEEK: A DIRECTOR'S GRATITUDE
variants.text: The bank opens on Monday, as usual, and its director, who has kept his key, his good name and his thirty thousand napoleons, sends you a box of cigars of such extraordinary quality that Watson, who is a connoisseur, cannot at first believe that they are a gift. You say that you do not smoke cigars. You give them to Lestrade.

ENDING_THE_ADDER_AT_THE_INQUEST.title: The Adder at the Inquest
ENDING_THE_ADDER_AT_THE_INQUEST.headline: SURREY DOCTOR COMMITTED FOR TRIAL: THE EVIDENCE IN A SACK
ENDING_THE_ADDER_AT_THE_INQUEST.text: It is produced on the second day of the inquest into Julia Stoner's death, in a closed wicker basket, with the coroner standing a good way back, and nothing in the course of the proceedings has so much effect. Dr Grimesby Roylott is committed for trial at the Assizes and does not at any point speak; he looks at the basket the whole of the time. He is condemned in July. Helen Stoner goes to her aunt at Harrow and is married in the autumn, and in the year after sends you, by post, a small, plain, extremely unexpected present: a pair of good, thick gloves.

variants.headline: THE ADDER AT THE INQUEST: A WITNESS AT THE WINDOW
variants.text: It is produced on the second day of the inquest in a wicker basket, and the coroner stands a good way back. Dr Watson is called, gives his evidence in the clear, flat voice of an army surgeon, and is asked whether he was frightened. He says that he was extremely frightened, and that he would do it again. Dr Grimesby Roylott is committed for trial and condemned in July.

ENDING_THE_UNDERTAKING.title: The Undertaking
ENDING_THE_UNDERTAKING.headline: BOHEMIAN COURT: A PROMISE PUT IN WRITING
ENDING_THE_UNDERTAKING.text: The King signs at Baker Street, in the kind of fury that does a man credit, with the mask on the table and a sulky Chancellor at his elbow. He undertakes in writing to leave Mrs Norton unmolested for the rest of her life. She undertakes, with her own signature and a seal in violet wax, that the photograph will be put away for ever in the safe of a firm in Lincoln's Inn. Nobody is humiliated. The betrothal is announced in June. In the summer there comes to Baker Street a note, on violet paper, that says: 'Quite so. I.N.' It is, you think, a signal that the treaty has been ratified.

ENDING_THE_GOOSE_CLUB.title: The Whole of the Goose Club
ENDING_THE_GOOSE_CLUB.headline: A CHRISTMAS DINNER AT BAKER STREET: THE COUNTESS'S STONE RESTORED
ENDING_THE_GOOSE_CLUB.text: By the second course it is quite clear that nobody at the table is going to be hanged, and by the fourth that nobody is going to be sorry. The blue carbuncle goes back to the Countess of Morcar with a covering note from Mr Sherlock Holmes, and John Horner the plumber is paid, out of the reward, the better part of what it cost him to be in prison. James Ryder goes to Canada in the spring with a letter of introduction from a gentleman in Museum Street who keeps a goose-club, and keeps, on the whole, remarkably straight. You tell Watson that you have never known the season of forgiveness so thoroughly overdone.

variants.headline: THE WHOLE OF THE GOOSE CLUB: A WIDOW'S DINNER
variants.text: Mrs Oakshott of the Brixton Road, who reared the geese and has not been so far from Brixton since her wedding, tells the table what a goose will and will not swallow, and Ryder is the only man present who is seen to take notes. The stone goes back to the Countess, and the reward to the plumber, and Ryder to Canada.

ENDING_THE_UMBRELLA.title: The Pawnbroker's Umbrella
ENDING_THE_UMBRELLA.headline: PAWNBROKER FELLS NOTORIOUS CRIMINAL IN OWN CELLAR
ENDING_THE_UMBRELLA.text: John Clay is taken in the cellar of the pawnbroker's shop in Saxe-Coburg Square at ten past ten on a Saturday night by a stout and trembling gentleman with an umbrella, and is carried out by Mr Peter Jones of Scotland Yard feeling, as he says, much more insulted than hurt. His accomplice is taken in the tunnel by three police. Jabez Wilson is the toast of the City for a week, is presented with a handsome umbrella by the directors of the City and Suburban Bank, and is asked by three separate newspapers to describe his feelings. He says that he does not at all know what they were. He says that they were red.

variants.headline: THE PAWNBROKER'S UMBRELLA: THE YARD AT THE FOOT OF THE STAIRS
variants.text: John Clay is taken in a pawnbroker's cellar by a stout gentleman with an umbrella, and Mr Peter Jones, who has been waiting four years to put his hand upon the man's collar, is just in time to put it there. He is exceedingly gracious about the umbrella. The directors of the City and Suburban Bank present Mr Wilson with another.
